long_biography.plain_text:
Von Boetticher trained and practised as a commercial lawyer, building an international Munich practice. He also founded KanAm, which developed property funds and real-estate investment services, and joined Dietmar Müller-Elmau and Keith Gruen in creating Fidelio. The hotel-management software became an international platform before MICROS acquired the remaining company in 1995.

He used the resulting investment base across publishing, property and hospitality. He bought and restructured Luchterhand and Volk & Welt, backed the revived Abendzeitung, and developed Orania.Berlin in a building he owned. Alongside these ventures, he established Gestüt Ammerland, breeding leading racehorses and later serving as president of the Munich racing association.

A secondary biographical directory gives Posen, now Poznań in Poland, as his birthplace, while a United States government document describes him as born in Germany in 1942, when Posen was under German annexation. The exact date is strongly corroborated, but no birthplace or birth-country proposal is made because modern geography and historical jurisdiction conflict.

Companies House and United States government evidence establish German nationality. A commercial biography labels him American, apparently from his United States legal qualification, but official material identifies Michigan bar admission rather than United States citizenship. German is proposed as primary nationality; no secondary nationality is inferred.

Tagesspiegel attributes his fortune chiefly to both fund advisory and Fidelio, while taz points to patent rights and real estate. Because strong evidence supports materially important technology and real-estate investment mechanisms without a reliable split, Diversified is used rather than forcing either Finance & Investments, Technology or Real Estate alone.

Berliner Zeitung describes von Boetticher as belonging to a historic noble family, but no strong source identifies inherited money, land, a family company or a transfer as the principal source of his wealth. Self-made reflects documented founder and professional mechanisms; it is not an inference that his upbringing lacked advantages.
